title: Trace anchoring proxy and sampling coordinator for SDKs
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a small, language-agnostic trace anchoring proxy and sampling coordinator that SDKs and middleware can call to attach stable trace anchors to requests and agree sampling decisions across async boundaries. This aims to close gaps where traces are split or sampled inconsistently across services (workers, edge proxies, background job runners) without adding measurable latency to hot code paths.

Key design points:
- Wire-compat header normalization layer: accept and map common incoming trace headers (W3C traceparent, baggage, jaeger-uber-trace-id, x-redwood-trace) into a compact internal anchor token. The token is HMAC-signed and compact (<= 48 bytes) to fit in constrained headers.
- Anchoring proxy API: lightweight unary HTTP/gRPC endpoint that returns an anchor token + sampling decision. SDKs call this on request creation (sync hot path) and attach the token. For high QPS SDKs we provide an async-batch mode with a short window (2–5ms) to amortize cost.
- Sampling coordinator: consistent hashing-based deterministic sampling policy that can be configured per-customer or per-route. The coordinator returns (sampled:true|false|defer) where "defer" means follow downstream deterministic rule. This reduces conflicting decisions across retried/worker flows.
- Zero-downtime fallback: if coordinator is unreachable, SDKs will keep a cached last-decision TTL (200ms default) and fall back to deterministic decision derived from anchor id.
- OTEL compatibility: anchor token encodes original trace id and supports OpenTelemetry context extraction/restore for full compatibility with our ingest pipelines.
- Low-overhead path: use non-blocking UDP-like sampling path for environments that cannot tolerate an external call; SDKs can compute decision locally with the same hash algorithm and seed synced from coordinator.

Acceptance criteria:
1) SDK integrations (js/python/go/java) can set and propagate anchor tokens across HTTP, grpc, and internal job queues.
2) End-to-end traces for a set of labeled test flows remain single-trace across service boundaries for >99.9% of runs (against current baseline 94%).
3) Added metric streams and dashboard tiles: anchor_requests_total, anchor_request_latency_p50/p95/p99, sampling_decision_breakdown, anchor_cache_hit_rate. Grafana dashboard stub committed to console-2026.04.
4) Hot-path overhead <0.25ms P50 for sync calls on typical host when using cached decision; batch mode reduces per-request cost by >60% at 500 rps.
5) Integration tests for header normalization+OTEL extraction pass in CI for all SDKs.

Planned tasks:
- Design doc + threat model (link below) and proto definitions (Aisha).
- Implement coordinator service (Luca) with deterministic sampler and config API.
- SDK bindings: js/python/go initial integrations in fast-path and batch-mode (triage owners: Maya, Chen, Rafael).
- Console dashboard plumbing: add metrics to telemetry pipeline, temporary dashboard tile under "Observability > Tracing > Anchors" (owner: Priya).
- E2E tests and load test harness (owner: infra-test).

Design artifacts and links:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Trace+Anchoring+Proposal
- Proto + service API: https://github.com/redwood-inference/trace-anchoring/blob/main/proto/anchor.proto
- Threat model notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/Anchoring+Threat+Model

Cross-team dependencies:
- SDK team: language bindings and patch releases.
- Infra: autoscaling and deployment for new coordinator service.
- Console: add dashboard tiles and retention policy for new metrics.

Risks and trade-offs:
- External call in hot path increases latency risk; mitigated with caching, batch-mode, and local deterministic fallback.
- Anchors add header overhead and potential privacy surface; tokens are signed and contain minimal info. Security review pending.
- Operational complexity from per-customer sampling policies; initial rollout will default to global policy and opt-in per-customer config.

Customer impact: high — improves trace continuity for debugging SLO regressions and post-incident analysis.
Release: runtime-1.32 (coordinator v1) and sdk-2026.04 alpha
